title: ID0412756-DC/Si-D/DE[Energu] - IVECO trucks
description:
Reported behaviour/issue:
IVECO not charging properly?
Solution:
Update 14/Mar/2025 - Catalina is already working on this, ticket opened for documentation purposes only
Update 17/Mar/2025 - Tomorrow 18th March, we will test on-site with IVECO trucks in Energu with the assistance of IVECO and customer.
Update 28/Mar/2025 - Call with IVECO this week shows that there might be something wrong with the EV. The reported “previous versions were working” turned out to be false, we downgraded the version to v5.0.23 and even though we could reach CableCheck in the first 5 sessions, the ones after all failed in the same manner as the ones in v6.
Update 31/Mar/2025  Call with Iveco tomorrow 1st April to follow up on both sides' progress . Waiting for R&D to provide us a reply for the IMD
Update 2/Apr/2025 - Call with IVECO revealed that for the CableCheck problems it's a very sensitive problem on their side where they close the session. We will check with RC-DE to go on site to perform measurements with the osciloscope
Update 4/Apr/2025 - HQ & RC will go to site on the 10th Apr to do osciloscope tests, IVECO will also participate?
Update from site intervention - We did not see the voltage spikes as IVECO mentioned and the SDP request is still missing
Update from 16/Apr - Why is it working in charger jERN9L in Munchen but not in Mauersteten? Collected the logs and investigation started
Update from 12/May - IVECO R&D is in discussions with EcoG directly
Update from 13/May - IVECO R&D acknowledged that the EVCC is shutting down - no root cause yet.
Update from 20/May - installed v7.0.5 with EcoG 1.4.12 - IVECO doesnt see any problem
Update from 6/june - Ecog to have a final discussion with IVECO, looks like EV issue so nothing for us to, final answer on 12/Jun
Update from 17/June -
So far we haven’t received any update from Iveco side about the root cause of the EVCC shutting down.
Update from 25/June -
I just received this feedback from Iveco colleagues:
“ Unfortunately, we didn’t receive any further insights about that from our previous EVCC supplier, except what I already told you.
At the moment, we’ve decided to upload another calibration on the two EVCC of our customer which own the Siemens charger with that issue and the charging seems working.”

RE: AW: Regarding Charging Tests in V-Markt CRM:00583000005
additional_info.body:
Dear Leandro,
I wanted to share with you our overview of the results from the tests you conducted yesterday with the IVECO trucks and the SiCharge D chargers at the customer V Markt site, accompanied by a Siemens expert remotely.
The vehicle used was the IVECO LKW S-eWAY, brought to the customer site from the IVECO Workshop in Memmingen.
The vehicle was tested with the SiCharge D300 (FW v6.1.3 - EcoG Layer 1.4.11 (with hot fix)) and SiCharge D160 (FW v6.1.3 - EcoG Layer 1.4.5 (without hot fix)).
Unfortunately, all charging attempts failed. The failures occurred at different stages, but all during the initialization.
Several observations were made, which were present in both chargers (with and without the hot-fix):
We observed the average attenuation of the frequency carrier groups is too high in some cases.
No SLAC PARAM RES
No SLAC MATCH
No SDP Request
No TCP handshake
The root cause for these failed charging sessions is not yet clear to us. We are currently investigating this together with our R&D team and would be happy to get input from your side based on your ongoing investigations as well.
The situation is indeed very special because, as you and the customer have already reported, the trucks were able to charge at other charging stations (Alpitronic and ABB).
However, we have the situation that Volvo trucks from the same customer can charge without problems at both their SiCharge D charging stations.
Moreover, I would like to add that the issue is present on both chargers, therefore the theory that the issues were brought up by the latest update (hot fix) cannot be confirmed.
I wanted to take this opportunity to ask you about a situation we identified at another customer site. We have identified another customer in Germany which also has IVECO trucks with MAC addresses
5c.cc.a0.02.62.9d, 5c.cc.a0.02.62.a5
&
5c.cc.a0.02.63.17
and is using SiCharge D to charge the trucks. The chargers have the same FW version as the SiCharge D300 at V Markt; however, at this other site, the issue discussed here is not occurring, and there are many successful charging sessions.
The question is whether you would be able to cross-check the FW version or technical specifications of those trucks and if there might be some difference to the trucks at V Markt that could be playing a role in the issues we have.
We will also be intersted in checking the Physical connection of the cable connector to the vehicle inlet. We would like to test the integrity of the CP line and PP line and connection when the truck is plugged in to discard any possible HW issues. let us know your thought on this and if we could organize a join onsit session for this purpose.
I look forward to your feedback and further collaboration on resolving this challenge.
Attached you can find the PLC traces of some of the tests sessions captured at the Sicharge D300 charger.
Kind regards
Catalina Mora

additional_info.subject: 0412756 - ID0412756-DC/Si-D/DE[Energu] - IVECO trucks CRM:00315002504
additional_info.body:
Hi colleagues, good afternoon. I hope you are doing well today.
In case you were not aware, there is a problem in V-markt (Energu) related to IVECO trucks. We had some discussions since the past month with the IVECO colleagues, also, and we want to plan a site visit to confirm our findings.
The customer complained that the IVECOs were no longer charging after the update to v6.0.3 or after updating the EcoG with the latest version (wakeup function for Volvos).
The common issue is that the IVECO trucks are not sending the SLAC requests properly and as such we cannot even go to Authentication and fails.
We downgraded the charger D300 (170002000) to v5.0.23 and we still found the same issues as before. So in theory, it's not a problem with the FW since we tested all these scenarios: v5.0.23, v6.0.3 with and without hotfix, v6.1.3 with and without hotfix.
They also complained that they were seeing some voltage raises on their circuit but we already aligned with R&D and the voltage that we are introducing in the circuit from the IMD, is not sufficient enough for their values. To be 100% clear, we are introducing this voltage from DC+ to PE and DC- to PE, not between DC+ and DC-, this is confirmed with the Voltage transducer readings.
Here is a image from the technical data sheet from the supplier.
IVECO is complaining that they are seeing values in the range of 60V and we are only applying at most 45V.
From our side, it's clear that the FW is not the answer.
We checked in a different customer (Janssen), where they also use the same EV model and software (reported by IVECO) and it's somewhat working, so we are able to pass the SLAC but there are still some failures in CableCheck.
Both these issues have been already acknowledged by IVECO and they are working towards a solution, both 60V issue and CableCheck.
The product is working as expected and correctly, based on the investigations performed so far, with the assistance of R&D themselves.
The idea here is that RC-DE goes to site with an osciloscope and measure the IMD and Voltage transducer readings, to prove that the issue lies on the IVECO-side or at worst case scenario, something in this particular location.
We are in discussion with the IVECO colleagues to align on a date to perform this task. At first, the proposed date would be on next Thursday, 10th April, please be free to share your agenda and if you want to change this date, we can align later.
This case is a priority since customer warned that he could replace the charger if we cannot find a solution fast enough, since he is using competitors' chargers to charge the IVECOs.
What equipment do you have to do these measurements?
I will wait for your feedback.
Best regards,
Francisco

Would this be possible from your side? We would like to perform the test on both the D160 and D300 chargers using your IVECO truck. We estimate the testing will take around 2 hours per charger.
If this works for you, could you please let us know your preferred start time for the test?
We understand the IVECO team is also planning to be onsite the same day, and they mentioned they will contact you directly on this matter.
Thank you very much. We look forward to your feedback.
Kind regards
Catalina Mora

Quick feedback from our side regarding this IVECO trucks issue:
There is a protocol called Home Plug AV which is responsible for certain parts of the PLC communication.
We found that the IVECO truck has a variable timeout for this protocol which sometimes causes the sessions to fail. We could see that some sessions that worked, had a bigger timeout (of around 200ms) and the ones that failed had a very small timeout (of around 3ms). This is an unusual behaviour.
This is being currently investigated between IVECO's R&D team and EcoG (which is our SECC supplier).
This Thursday, we have a short meeting with the EcoG team and hopefully we will have more information to provide you.
Thank you for your patience and helpfulness so far.

Hi Martin, good afternoon.
Quick feedback from our side regarding this IVECO trucks issue:
There is a protocol called Home Plug AV which is responsible for certain parts of the PLC communication.
We found that the IVECO truck has a variable timeout for this protocol which sometimes causes the sessions to fail. We could see that some sessions that worked, had a bigger timeout (of around 200ms) and the ones that failed had a very small timeout (of around 3ms). This is an unusual behaviour.
This is being currently investigated between IVECO's R&D team and EcoG (which is our SECC supplier).
This Thursday, we have a short meeting with the EcoG team and hopefully we will have more information to provide you.
Thank you for your patience and helpfulness so far.
Best regards,
Francisco
